title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a single sketch, headed X_2^*, drawn on the back of a computer printout. Read with the title of the cote, it illustrates the 'déploiement' (unfolding) of a stratified space.

The simplest reading takes as model a 2-dimensional stratified space with three strata:
- X_0 = a point x_0;
- X_1 = an arc or half-line issuing from x_0;
- X_2 = the open complement in the plane.

The unfolding X^* replaces each stratum X_i by a manifold with boundary or corners X_i^*. Its boundary pieces are indexed by chains of strata i<j<..., and each boundary piece fibres over the lower stratum with fibre the link.

In the sketch:
- x_0 = x_0^*: the point stratum is unchanged under unfolding.
- The circle: it should be read as the deleted neighbourhood of x_0. Its boundary is the link circle, i.e. the stratum x_0 blown up into its link.
- x_{01}: the point where the 1-stratum meets that link. It is a corner of type (0,1) and is also the endpoint of X_1^*.
- \underline{x}_1: the middle strand, i.e. X_1^*, a closed half-line.
- x_{12} (twice): the upper and lower strands are the two lifts of X_1 into the boundary of X_2^*. Cutting the plane open along the 1-stratum produces two boundary copies, because the link of X_1 in X_2 is two points.

So X_2^* is the plane with x_0 blown up to a circle and slit along X_1. Its boundary is (circle) ∪ (two copies of the half-line), meeting at corners above x_{01}. This is the basic example showing that the unfolding of the top stratum covers the lower strata with fibres equal to the links (here S^1 over x_0 and two points over X_1). It fits a programme of replacing stratified spaces by diagrams of manifolds with corners, which would yield the conical (tubular) neighbourhoods and the homotopy type of the stratified space.
errors: No mathematical errors detectable. The sketch is schematic: the two 'x_12' strands and the slit are drawn without explicit corners at the circle, so the corner structure (over x_{01}) is implicit.

ideas.what: Unfolding (déploiement) of a stratified space: each stratum replaced by a manifold with boundary/corners whose boundary strata are indexed by chains of strata and fibre over lower strata via links. Illustrated on a planar example (point ⊂ half-line ⊂ plane).
ideas.modern_name: Resolution / unfolding / 'décollement' of a Thom–Mather stratified space; 'unzipping' of conically smooth stratified spaces; manifolds with corners associated to Thom–Mather control data
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather (control data, 1969–70); Verona (resolution of stratified spaces, 1984); Brasselet–Hector–Saralegi (décollement, 1990s); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (unzip, 2017)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5 'théorie de Galois-Teichmüller' and the 'Géométrie modérée' section, mentions 'déploiement' of tame stratified spaces in outline only

missed.claim: The notes contain an explicit worked picture of the unfolding of the simplest non-trivial 2-dimensional stratification. It records the indexing of boundary pieces by chains of strata (x_{01}, x_{12}), anticipating the later 'unzip'/décollement formalism. This is only a pedagogical illustration of a known idea, not a new result.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents that Grothendieck's 1981–82 déploiement (sketched in the Esquisse) concretely meant the chain-indexed manifold-with-corners resolution, now standard via Verona and Ayala–Francis–Tanaka. It is of historical interest only.

deep.surprise_reason: A single illustrative sketch of a standard construction (blow up the point to its link, cut open along the 1-stratum). The construction is known in the literature and announced in the Esquisse, so no new mathematics is visible on the page.
transcription_corrections: The circle is better read as the blown-up neighbourhood of x_0 (link circle) than as a generic disc. The middle strand label is \underline{x}_1 (the label has a dot/blot), and x_{01} is the point where the middle strand meets the circle.
The background typed text is bleed-through from a computer printout (VAR(1), VAR(2), Y(I) values) and is not part of the notes.
